To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) E2F1 suppresses cell cycle activity in mature neurons, and 2) in its absence, neurons cycle, divide, and die.
E2F1 works as a cell cycle repressor in mature neurons.
(1) E2f1 is a suppressor of the cell cycle in mature neurons and (2) E2f−/− neurons cycle in vivo and in vitro, whereas E2f+/− neurons cycle in vitro but not in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the cell cycle is controlled in neurons.
how cells are able to maintain a nondividing, differentiated state.
the mechanisms that regulate the cell cycle in mature neurons and the consequences of cell cycle reactivation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
E2f1 functions to prevent cell cycle initiation in mature neurons.
E2F1 works as a cell cycle supressor in mature neurons.
E2F1 acts as a cell cycle repressor in neurons and that the absence of E2F1 leads to the initiation of the cell cycle and cell cycle-related death.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the absence of E2f-1, neurons are no longer restricted to a single cell division.
E2F1 acts as a suppressor of cell division in mature CNS neurons.
E2f1 acts in the brain as a tumor suppressor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, although the cell cycle machinery remains intact in mature neurons, the E2F1 transcription factor is required to prevent the cell cycle from being initiated in the absence of extrinsic cues.
E2F1 acts in mature neurons to suppress cell division.
E2f1 is not required for the cell cycle initiation that precedes cell death of cerebellum granule neurons in the lurcher and staggerer mouse mutants.
